extracted.intended_audience: Wikisource contributors and readers looking for authoritative editions/transcriptions of Novum Organum
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance and metadata for presenting, verifying, and citing Francis Bacon's Novum Organum on Wikisource, including edition/translation selection and public-domain status. Focuses on source verification, preferred citation practice, and noting editorial differences between translations/editions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Provide scanned source for verification
rubrics_metrics.description: "This work is not backed by a scanned copy of the edition from which it was transcribed. Please see this document's talk page for details for verification. 'Source' means a location at which other users can find a copy of this work. Ideally this will be a scanned copy of the original that can be uploaded to Wikimedia Commons and proofread."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Where possible, supply a scanned copy of the original edition used for transcription so others can verify the text. If a scan is not available, explain the situation on the page's talk page and give a clear 'Source' location where users can find the edition. Upload scans to Wikimedia Commons and mark the transcription as proofread when appropriate. Anti-pattern: leaving no source information or unverifiable transcription without explanation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Preferred citation practice / edition
rubrics_metrics.description: "The Spedding edition printed in London ... is generally the standard for scholarly citation, but citation by section, book, and aphorism, instead of volume and page, is frequently more useful and now widely accepted."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For scholarly citation of Novum Organum, prefer the Spedding edition when possible. However, citing by internal divisions (section, book, aphorism) is often more useful and is widely accepted — use these structural citations to help readers locate passages across editions. Scoring note: preference toward using standard scholarly editions and clear structural citations rather than inconsistent page/volume references.

rubrics_metrics.name: Document editorial history and differences between translations/editions
rubrics_metrics.description: The page documents multiple 19th-century translations and notes editorial interventions: e.g., "The translation was done by an unnamed Cambridge undergraduate and then finalized by Spedding. Though sometimes loose and affected, it is also at times elegant." and "After some Americanization of spelling, punctuation, and phrasing, it was used in the fourteen-volume edition..."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When presenting a translation, record who translated/edited it and note substantive editorial changes (americanization of spelling, punctuation, omitted sections such as dedications, added footnotes). Provide edition-specific notes so readers understand textual differences. Example: note whether footnotes present in an edition are reproduced; indicate if certain preliminary materials (dedication, preface) are omitted. Anti-pattern: presenting a translation without noting its editorial provenance or alterations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Include edition-specific apparatus when available (footnotes, prefaces, dedications)
rubrics_metrics.description: "Devey added many footnotes (not reproduced here). His editions did not include the dedication."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If an edition contains footnotes, prefaces, or other apparatus, indicate whether those elements are included in the transcription and, if omitted, mention that explicitly. Prefer to reproduce scholarly apparatus where copyright allows, or link to scans/editions that include them. This helps users assess interpretive choices and variant readings.

rubrics_metrics.name: Verify public-domain/copyright status
rubrics_metrics.description: "This work was published before January 1, 1931, and is in the public domain worldwide because the author died at least 100 years ago."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Confirm and record the copyright status of the work and particular editions/translations before reuse or redistribution. For Novum Organum, the work and older 19th-century translations noted are public domain, but always verify for specific edition/translation. Guidance: include an explicit public-domain statement on the page when applicable; if not public domain, provide licensing info.

rubrics_metrics.name: Link to related resources and translations
rubrics_metrics.description: The page provides links to multiple translations and related projects (e.g., "There were four complete translations done in the 19th century. Three of them... are linked below." and links to Wikipedia, Commons, Wikidata).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide links to other translations, scans, and sister projects (Commons, Wikipedia, Open Library, Archive.org) so readers can consult alternate versions and supporting materials. This aids cross-checking and scholarship. Anti-pattern: isolated transcription with no links or references to alternate editions or scans.
